title: The Cash Tin

traces.label: Back window left unlatched
traces.text: The back window is pushed open. It was never latched.

traces.label: Cash tin gone from the counter
traces.text: The cash tin's gone. Frank says there was over £23 in it.

traces.label: Muddy bootprints
traces.prompt: Tap the floor near the window
traces.text: Mud, still wet. A big work boot with hobnails. Measure it?

measure.label: Size 10, hobnail sole
measure.text: Size 10, hobnail sole. A big man's work boot.

traces.label: Hobnail prints outside, towards the creek
traces.text: The same hobnail prints, coming from and going back towards the creek.

traces.label: Smaller prints along the bank
traces.text: Smaller prints, size 8, worn tread. They wander along the bank and never come near the store.

records.name: Credit ledger
records.text: PIKE, L. Owes £11 4s. Credit STOPPED Thursday. (in Frank's hand)

records.name: Exchange log
records.text: Only one call after 7:30 pm: 10:40 pm. Doyle residence to Ballarat 2214. Trunk call, 6 minutes.

r_frank.note: Owner of the store. Half the town owes him money.

statements.text: Locked the front door at half seven, went to the dance with Edna and June. Came back at twenty-five to eleven and the window was wide open.

press.text: Who'd do it? Half the town owes me money. Len Pike's the worst of them. Here, have a look at the ledger.

r_edna.note: Runs the exchange. Hears everything and says little.

statements.text: Exchange closed for the dance. Only one call all night, after we got home. Have a look at the log.

press.text: Mrs Doyle rang her sister. Sounded upset. I didn't listen in. Well, a little. She said, 'I don't know what to do, Win.'

r_agnes.note: Neighbour. Her kitchen window faces the store. Close to Marge Pike. Protecting someone?

statements.text: I didn't go to the dance. My knees aren't what they were.

press.text: I had my tea and listened to the wireless.

statements.text: I was in bed by nine, dear. I didn't hear a thing all night.

contradicted_by.result: All right. I was up. I... saw someone behind the store. A man in a hat, just after nine.

statements.text: It was dark. I couldn't say who.

contradicted_by.result: Big work boots... He walked like Len. God forgive me, Marge is my dearest friend.

r_halina.note: Dancing with her husband all evening. Notices things.

statements.text: We were at the dance all evening. Tomasz danced with me twice, which is a miracle.

press.text: Len? He went out around ten to nine. When he came back his trousers were muddy to here.

r_davey.note: Len's son. Sneaks off to smoke. Hiding something small.

statements.text: I was at the dance the whole time.

contradicted_by.result: Fine. I went down the creek for a smoke. Don't tell Mum.

statements.text: I never went near the store.

press.text: Saw Dad on the track, actually. Heading back to the shed. Said to mind my business.

r_len.note: Mill hand. Owes Frank money and hasn't told his wife.

statements.text: I was at the dance all night. Ask anyone.

contradicted_by.result: Went out for a smoke. Ten minutes.
Went out for a smoke. Ten minutes.

statements.text: Ten minutes, I was back by nine.

contradicted_by.result: She's an old woman, she sees things.

statements.text: I don't owe Hayward a penny he won't get back.

confession.text: He shamed me in front of my wife. In front of the whole town. I've got debts Marge doesn't know about. I just... I was going to put it back.

finds.label: Cash tin and size 10 hobnail boots under the woodpile
finds.text: The cash tin, £23 10s intact, under the woodpile, and Len's hobnail boots, size 10, still muddy.

deductions.sentence: The thief came in through the [entry].
The bootprints belong to someone with size [size] [sole] boots.
Len Pike left the dance between [from] and [to].
The size 8 prints never reached the store.

resolutions.label: Charge Len
resolutions.text: Len goes to the district court for 4 weeks. The Pikes' income drops.

resolutions.label: Restitution
resolutions.text: Len repays from his wages and does a month of community work.

tip: Residents have started latching their windows. A lamp behind the store wouldn't hurt either.
